Q: Dynamics plugin update record after create A: 
Entity postMessageEntity = (Entity)context.PostEntityImages["newbookpostImage"];

Is your PostEntityImage a new_books entity?

Also, if you have a postMessageEntity entity, you can directly get the Entity Record ID by

postMessageEntity.ID

rather than

Guid RecordID = ((Guid)postMessageEntity.Attributes["new_booksid"]);

Here, your code does nothing more than create empty object of type Entity new_books. You have not set the name field of the entity, or any other. Also, you have not created a record, you should use:

Entity created_book = new Entity("new_books")
service.Create(created_book);

Below, you are trying to fetch the Record from the Entity new_books based on postMessageEntity.Id.

created_book = service.Retrieve(created_book.LogicalName, RecordID, new ColumnSet(true));

You should check that the logical name of the postMessageEntity is the same as created_book.LogicalName and then use postMessageEntity.ID rather than RecordID.

Q: Is PyArrow Append Columns an In-Place Operation? A:

No, it’s not in-place.

table.append_column(...) creates a new Table object.

It does not duplicate the existing columns (a and b)

those are just referenced (shared memory).

However, the new column itself is newly allocated, so memory is used for 'COUNTRY_ID'.

Q: Is there a functionality in Java similar to C#'s anonymous types? A:

koppor shows ways that the language has evolved since this answer.

Preserving the answer below for the record, because it does correctly capture the relationship between the lack of a solution and the lack of a feature: a way to declare a variable whose type is inferred to be an unmentionable type.

----

No. There is no equivalent. There is no typeless variable declaration (var) in Java that the Java compiler could fill in with the auto-generated type name to allow a.Count and a.Message to be accessed.
